title: The Royal Family Runs on Rules You've Never Heard Of
beats: Starts at 1066, admitting the start point is arbitrary; William the Conqueror (Norman = French).
Family tree interface introduced; deliberately omits children who don't matter.
No formal rules yet: eldest-son advantage plus 'bigger-army diplomacy', a recurring gag-rule.
Henry I's oath for Matilda ignored; Stephen gets crowned first; civil war stalemate.
Henry II sees the failures and invents co-kingship, rule of two: one is none, two is one.
The fix backfires: apprentice rebels, another civil war; then a run of eldest-son successions.
Every arrow glosses complexity; Isabella deposes Edward II; Black Prince dies, Richard II.
Bigger-army diplomacy again; War of the Roses compressed to 'Henry VI, Edward IV, Henry VI, Edward IV. The end.'
Princes vanish, Richard III, Henry VII marries for legitimacy.
Henry VIII writes inheritance rules; Parliament approves; immediately undermined by Edward VI naming Lady Jane Grey.
Nine-day queen, Mary, Elizabeth; childless queens; 'Lady Jane Grey was next in... oh.'
Scotland's line joins the tree; James borrowed, two regnal numbers.
Cromwell abolishes monarchy; son breaks 'rule 0: keep the army happy'; restoration.
Catholic James II displaced by William and Mary via invited 'invasion'; Anne childless despite 17 pregnancies.
Parliament does a 'royal reboot' resetting all claims to Sophia of Hanover; rules finally stick.
Calm descent under the rules: the Georges, William IV, Victoria.
Edward VIII breaks the boring line by marrying a twice-divorced American; abdication.
George VI, Elizabeth II longest reign, line continues to Charles, William, George.

metrics.misconception: partly: that the line of succession was ever neat or rule-bound before 1701
metrics.brute_force: yes 0:35: succession by free-for-all and force shown first, repeatedly failing before formal rules
metrics.examples: ~40 successions; grow from simple father-son to branch jumps, foreign merges, and a full reset
metrics.ending: Calm modern line to Prince George; no recap

principles.6: confirmed: 0:35-6:36 the ad-hoc 'bigger army' method is shown failing over and over before the formal reset.
principles.7: confirmed: viewer sees disputes repeat until Parliament's reboot at 6:36 feels inevitable.

principles.10: partly: chronology, not complexity, drives order, though branches grow messier.
principles.11: confirmed: rules-free era, failed fixes, final rules, ordered so the payoff is earned.

theory: The video is really an argument for why formal succession rules exist, told as 650 years of the brute-force alternative failing. By letting the viewer watch ad-hoc succession and patch-fixes collapse repeatedly on one persistent family-tree interface, the 1701 'royal reboot' lands as an earned solution rather than a fact.
velocity: Orchestrator playbook 'failed-fix ladder': show the naive method, then 2-3 patches failing, before revealing the robust rule.
Scene builder: one persistent, growing tree/graph; prune visibly and narrate what was cut.
Voice: compress repetitive stretches into a rhythmic list to let the pattern itself be the message.
Learner model: track coined shorthand terms (like 'bigger-army diplomacy') and reuse them as explanatory variables.
Evals: ask why Parliament needed the Sophia reset; correct answers cite the repeated failures, not the date.
quote: one is none. Two is one.
